beats.lead: Everyone's heard that humans only use 10% of their brain
beats.text: and everyone's heard it was Einstein who said so.
beats.note: There is no real evidence Einstein ever said anything like it. The myth gets pinned on him because his name is shorthand for genius.

beats.name: Lowell Thomas
beats.role: A broadcaster who wrote the foreword to Dale Carnegie's 'How to Win Friends and Influence People', attributing a precise '10 percent' figure to psychologist William James, who had only ever made a much vaguer claim decades earlier.

beats.note: PET and fMRI scans show every region of the brain active to some degree at all times, even during sleep. Damage almost anywhere causes a loss of function.

beats.context: Share of the body's total energy the brain burns, despite being only about 2% of its weight. Evolution should have deleted a genuinely unused 90%, not preserved it.

beats.text: In 2010, MythBusters measured brain activity during a hard mental task with real medical scanners. They found up to 35% active at once, comfortably clearing the mythical 10%.

beats.line: The 90% you're 'not using' is switched on right now, reading this.
